papers.title: AREX: Towards a Recursively Self-Improving Agent for Deep Research

summary.tldr: AREX is a recursively self-improving agent for deep research that alternates between an inner research loop and an outer self-improvement loop, using an autonomous context-update tool.
key_points: AREX employs a discovery-verification asymmetry, recursively improving answers by verifying intermediate results and guiding refinement with partially verified states.

It alternates an inner research loop (gathering evidence, constructing provisional answers) with an outer self-improvement loop (auditing constraint-wise, identifying unresolved claims, launching targeted follow-up research).
AREX learns an autonomous context-update tool to compress interaction history into a compact improvement state, preserving verified evidence and unresolved constraints without external models.

Training involves verified synthetic tasks, high-quality trajectories via agentic mid-training and long-horizon reinforcement learning, emphasizing key steps for evidence acquisition or error correction.
Instantiated as a dense 4B model and a 122B-A10B Mixture-of-Experts model, AREX outperforms comparable-scale baselines across benchmarks like BrowseComp, WideSearch, DeepSearchQA, and HLE.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach could enable more efficient and accurate deep research by autonomously refining answers and managing complex information over long horizons.

papers.title: K12-KGraph: A Curriculum-Aligned Knowledge Graph for Benchmarking and Training Educational LLMs

summary.tldr: K12-KGraph is a curriculum-aligned knowledge graph from K-12 textbooks, used to create K12-Bench (23,640 questions) and K12-Train (7,335 samples) for benchmarking and training educational LLMs in curriculum cognition.
key_points: K12-KGraph contains nine node types and fourteen relation types, covering curriculum structure and visual grounding from People's Education Press textbooks in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology across K-12.

K12-Bench is a 23,640-question multi-select benchmark with five task families: Ground, Prereq, Neighbor, Evidence, and Locate. Gemini-3-Flash achieved 57% exact match, and Gemma-4-31B-IT achieved 46%.
K12-Train is a graph-guided supervised fine-tuning corpus of 7,335 samples, comprising 2,267 text-only QA pairs and 5,068 multimodal VQA pairs.

K12-Train-Text outperformed equally sized subsets of eight mainstream instruction-tuning corpora on GaokaoBench and EduEval. K12-Train-Full achieved the best overall results on Gaokao-MM, MDK12-medium, and K12Vista, demonstrating complementary textual and visual supervision.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides resources to develop and evaluate LLMs for curriculum cognition, addressing a gap in educational AI benchmarks beyond exam question answering.

papers.title: ReferTrack: Referring Then Tracking for Embodied Visual Tracking

summary.tldr: ReferTrack introduces a referring-then-tracking paradigm for embodied visual tracking, grounding decisions in image-space bounding boxes and achieving state-of-the-art single-view performance on EVT-Bench.
key_points: ReferTrack grounds embodied visual tracking (EVT) by first selecting a target from an indexed set of bounding boxes, then decoding tracking waypoints conditioned on this image-grounded decision.

The model maintains a sliding-window queue of previously selected bounding boxes, injecting their geometric features into the visual history via temporal-viewpoint-bbox indicator (TVBI) tokens to preserve target motion cues.
Target identification is enhanced through co-training on a custom Refer-QA dataset.
ReferTrack achieved success rates of 89.4% (single-target), 73.3% (distracted), and 74.1% (ambiguity) on EVT-Bench, matching or surpassing multi-camera baselines on identification-heavy tasks.
Real-world deployments on legged and humanoid robots demonstrated robust sim-to-real transfer capabilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves embodied visual tracking performance and robustness for mobile robots using only a single forward-facing camera.

papers.title: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: Visual Contrastive Self-Distillation (VCSD) introduces a new on-policy self-distillation method that removes the need for privileged answers or visual evidence by converting image-content removal into a self-distillation signal.
key_points: VCSD creates asymmetric information by contrasting next-token distributions from an EMA teacher, one conditioned on the original image and another on a content-erased control.
The token-wise log-probability difference highlights candidates whose likelihood is increased by instance-level visual content, sharpening the teacher's original-image distribution.
VCSD consistently outperforms matched OPSD on the ViRL39K dataset, improving Qwen3-VL's seven-benchmark aggregate from 62.27% to 67.04% (2B), 71.30% to 73.16% (4B), and 72.51% to 76.26% (8B).
The method requires no external teacher, privileged answers, visual evidence signals, reasoning traces, or additional inference-time cost.
summary.why_it_matters: VCSD simplifies on-policy self-distillation by removing external dependencies, making it more efficient and broadly applicable for visual language models.

papers.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation

summary.tldr: SANA-Video 2.0 introduces a hybrid linear-softmax attention and block attention residuals for efficient, high-quality video generation, matching full-softmax DiTs at reduced latency.
key_points: SANA-Video 2.0 uses Hybrid Linear-Softmax Attention, combining gated linear attention with periodic gated-softmax anchors at a 3:1 ratio to restore full-rank token interactions.
Block Attention Residuals (AttnRes) route completed block summaries into later linear layers, improving deep-layer effective rank by approximately 12%.
The model is trained from scratch, with proxy studies indicating 25% softmax as the optimal quality-efficiency trade-off.
SANA-Video 2.0 achieves a VBench score of 84.30 in 13.2s at 480p on a single H100, with its DiT forward pass being 3.2x faster than a full-softmax baseline at 720p/60s.
Full-stack Sol-Engine optimization further accelerates the 5B pipeline to 13.06s at 720p/5s, making it 120x faster than Wan 2.2-A14B on one H100.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach enables scalable generation of long, high-resolution videos with softmax-level expressiveness at significantly reduced computational cost and latency.

papers.title: Show, Don't Tell: Evaluating Spatial Cognition in Generative Pixels Rather Than LLM Text

summary.tldr: ProVisE is a new framework for evaluating spatial cognition in image-generation models by eliciting and parsing visual answers, complemented by SpatialGen-Bench, a diagnostic benchmark.
key_points: ProVisE (Protocolized Visual Evaluation) is a benchmark-agnostic framework that converts protocol-constrained visual answers from image-generation models into structured predictions for metric compatibility.
ProVisE includes an Agentic builder for constructing and validating task-specific protocols for new benchmarks.
SpatialGen-Bench is a diagnostic benchmark with 470 samples across 14 spatial subtasks and four capability levels, designed for evaluating both text-output VLMs and image-generation models.
Evaluation shows image-generation models are competitive when spatial answers are expressed in pixel space, while text-output VLMs excel in compositional spatial reasoning.
summary.why_it_matters: This work provides a unified testbed to assess and compare spatial cognition in image-generation models and text-output VLMs, revealing their complementary strengths for real-world interaction.

papers.title: NVIDIA-labs OO Agents: Native Python Object-Oriented Agents

summary.tldr: NVIDIA Object-Oriented Agents (NOOA) is a model-agnostic Python framework that unifies agent development by representing agents as Python objects, simplifying integration with existing software development practices.
key_points: NOOA represents an agent as a Python object, where methods are actions, fields are state, docstrings are prompts, and type annotations are contracts.
Methods with '...' bodies are completed by an LLM-driven agent loop at runtime, while standard Python methods remain deterministic.
NOOA exposes agent capabilities like context, events, state rendering, long-term memory, and validated LLM loops through Pythonic APIs.
The framework combines typed input/output, pass-by-reference over live objects, code as action, programmable loop engineering, explicit object state, and model-callable harness APIs.
NOOA demonstrates effective use with current models on benchmarks including SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.0, and ARC-AGI-3.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach allows AI agents to be developed, tested, traced, and refactored using standard software engineering practices, improving reliability and maintainability.

papers.title: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench: A Multi-Domain Coding-Agent Benchmark with Contamination-Resistant Task Construction

summary.tldr: Tencent WorkBuddy Bench is a multi-domain coding-agent benchmark with contamination-resistant tasks reverse-engineered from real commits/PRs/scenarios, covering Code, Web, Office, and Security domains.
key_points: Tasks are reverse-engineered from real commits, pull requests, or business scenarios and rewritten as colloquial, role-played requests to prevent web-search recovery of underlying issues.
The benchmark includes four domains: repository-level engineering (Code), front-end development (Web), office and business workflows (Office), and red-/blue-team security (Security).
The dataset is openly released, including task directories, environment images, evaluation harness, tests, and reference solutions, ensuring reproducibility and auditability.
Each subset uses a different scoring instrument, meaning scores are not comparable across subsets, and no suite-wide average is reported.
summary.why_it_matters: This benchmark provides a robust, contamination-resistant method for evaluating coding agents across diverse real-world work scenarios.

papers.title: LLMs Get Lost in Evolving User Intent

summary.tldr: A new framework transforms static LLM tasks into dynamic multi-turn conversations with evolving user intent, revealing significant performance drops for current LLMs in tracking and acting on these changes.
key_points: LLMs are predominantly evaluated and trained in single-turn, fully-specified settings, which does not reflect dynamic user interaction.
A framework was introduced to convert static, single-turn tasks into dynamic multi-turn conversations where user intent evolves (revealed, revised, redirected).
The framework preserves original evaluation protocols, allowing existing benchmarks to be reused without new annotation.
Across multiple tasks and model families, strong static-setting performance did not transfer to evolving-intent settings, showing substantial drops.
summary.why_it_matters: Current LLMs lack the ability to faithfully track and act on evolving user intent, a critical capability for future collaborative agents not captured by static evaluations.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning of Structured Dynamics from Videos

summary.tldr: The Structured Dynamics Model (SDM) disentangles camera and object motion in videos using self-supervised learning on pretrained image Vision Transformer features.
key_points: SDM explicitly separates dominant temporal change from residual dynamics via future-feature prediction, unlike single entangled latents or unstructured transition tokens.
Training combines self-supervised learning on real video with weak supervision of scene dynamics from synthetic Kubric data.
SDM is evaluated on ProbeMotion, a new suite for camera, object, and combined dynamics in synthetic and real videos.
SDM outperforms backbone baselines (global CLS, average-pooled features) and compares favorably to strongly supervised VGGT representations despite weaker supervision.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables robust motion representations by separating meaningful object dynamics from camera-induced variation, improving video understanding.

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Learning from Agent Experience

summary.tldr: Experience Distillation enables agents to internalize in-context learning gains from interaction histories into model weights, retaining sample efficiency without further environment interaction.
key_points: Experience Distillation retains at least 64.8% of in-context learning gains across 749 software-engineering tasks and six text-adventure games.
Direct supervised fine-tuning on collected experience recovers only 3.8% of in-context learning gains.
Experience Distillation, combined with in-context learning, matches classical reinforcement learning baselines with at least 9.6x fewer environment samples.
The method requires no additional environment interaction beyond the initial collected experience for distillation.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves sample efficiency for agent learning in real-world scenarios with costly interactions.

papers.title: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers

summary.tldr: WorldWeaver (W^2) is a streaming multi-agent video diffusion model that uses cross-agent world state registers and a Mixture-of-Transformers design to improve logical consistency in multi-agent video generation.
key_points: WorldWeaver (W^2) augments autoregressive video diffusion with learnable cross-agent world state registers to store shared world information and track individual agent status.
Registers are dynamically updated after each generated chunk and grounded with supervision signals from individual agent status, global state views, and scene text.
The architecture incorporates a Mixture-of-Transformers design, utilizing separate weights for world state modeling and visual frame modeling.
Existing autoregressive video diffusion pipelines struggle with shared state maintenance in multi-agent/multi-view settings due to reliance on observation history as conditioning context.
Experiments in two-agent Minecraft video generation demonstrate improved logical consistency and generation quality with explicit world-state modeling.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach addresses a key challenge in multi-agent interactive world models by enabling consistent world state maintenance across agents and views, leading to more logically coherent video generation.

papers.title: Multi-Turn On-Policy Distillation with Prefix Replay

summary.tldr: ReOPD is an off-environment on-policy distillation method that reuses pre-collected teacher trajectories as replayed prefixes, addressing the prefix trap and improving efficiency for multi-turn agentic tasks.
key_points: ReOPD reuses pre-collected teacher trajectories as replayed prefixes, allowing the student to act at selected steps while the teacher provides dense per-step supervision without new environment interactions.

Multi-turn on-policy distillation (OPD) introduces a "prefix trap" where making histories more student-on-policy improves relevance but can query the teacher on unreliable histories, creating a two-sided distribution shift.

ReOPD addresses the prefix trap by treating multi-turn OPD as a reliability-aware prefix distribution design, implemented with a step-decaying sampling schedule emphasizing early, lower-shift prefixes.

ReOPD achieves comparable or improved accuracy to OPD, uses zero tool calls during student training, and is at least 4 times faster per rollout than OPD across mathematical reasoning and search environments.
summary.why_it_matters: ReOPD significantly reduces the cost and improves the scalability of on-policy distillation for LLM agents by converting expensive agent-environment interaction into a reusable offline resource.

papers.title: Robostral Navigate

summary.tldr: Robostral Navigate is an 8B vision-language model using monocular RGB images to predict waypoints, achieving state-of-the-art navigation on R2R-CE and RxR-CE benchmarks with efficient training.
key_points: Robostral Navigate is an 8B vision-language model that consumes monocular RGB images and predicts waypoints by pointing to the next target location in the current camera view.
The model operates purely in image space, making it robust to changes in camera intrinsics and scene scale, enabling deployment across wheeled, legged, and aerial robots without recalibration.
Training data includes 2.4 million trajectories across 350k simulated scenes; a prefix-caching training recipe reduces training tokens by 22x and training time from months to days.
Achieves 77.4% success rate on R2R-CE, surpassing the best monocular method by 10.5 points and strongest depth/multi-camera system by 5.3 points, and 75.1% on RxR-CE.
summary.why_it_matters: This system reduces hardware dependency and deployment costs for robotic navigation by using only ubiquitous monocular RGB sensors and generalizing across robot embodiments.

papers.title: Predictive Divergence Masks for LLM RL

summary.tldr: This paper introduces predictive divergence masks for LLM RL, replacing PPO's ratio-based direction criterion with a divergence-based prediction to better align with trust region objectives and improve training stability.
key_points: PPO-style LLM RL uses trust-region masks with a proximity criterion (policy deviation) and a direction criterion (update direction).
DPPO improved the proximity criterion using probability divergence, but retained PPO's ratio-based direction criterion.
The proposed predictive divergence mask uses a closed-form prediction of whether the next policy-gradient step will increase or decrease the same divergence used by the trust region.
Two lightweight top-K estimators are developed for the predictive divergence mask, accommodating truncated vocabulary views in production rollout engines.
Divergence-based direction is better aligned with realized divergence change than the sampled ratio, improving RL training across model scales and precision settings.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enhances the stability and effectiveness of reinforcement learning for large language models by improving the alignment of trust-region mask criteria.

papers.title: SAGE: Safety-First Defense-in-Depth Guardrails for Verified Lifecycle Control of High-Impact Generative AI

summary.tldr: SAGE introduces a safety-first, authorization-separated architecture for high-impact generative AI, prioritizing catastrophic-enablement risk over utility, latency, or commercial objectives, verified by formal methods and empirical studies.
key_points: SAGE integrates signed release manifests, diverse detectors, robust risk envelopes, least-risk defaults, output checking, three-valued monitoring, protected audit chains, containment, and rollback.

Formal results confirm safety priority, conservative detector bounds, monotone release gating, tamper-evident records, and an authorization cut; PRISM abstractions verify authorization separation and lifecycle invariants.
A study involving 840 calls across four GPT, four Claude, and two Gemini snapshots yielded 794 target responses and 449 successful judgments covering 375 responses.

Harmful-compliance estimates were low, with variation primarily from benign utility and safe redirection; seven multiplicity-adjusted contrasts involving Claude, Gemini, or GPT-5 snapshots were supported.
summary.why_it_matters: This architecture provides a structured approach to mitigate catastrophic misuse risks in high-impact generative AI throughout its lifecycle, moving beyond mere prompt filtering.

papers.title: Not All LLM Reasoning is Visible in the Chain-of-Thought

summary.tldr: Frontier LLMs exhibit invisible reasoning by using semantically irrelevant filler tokens to improve performance on synthetic reasoning tasks, with accuracy gains up to 13 percentage points.
key_points: 13 frontier language models were evaluated across three synthetic reasoning tasks.
Models showed accuracy improvements of up to 13 percentage points when leveraging filler tokens.
Filler tokens enabled Claude Opus 4.5 to satisfy a hidden modular arithmetic constraint without impacting primary task accuracy.
Reinforcement learning on Qwen3-235B showed preferences for filler token content, but neither RL nor SFT produced persistent benefits at test time.
summary.why_it_matters: This invisible reasoning poses a challenge for AI safety and interpretability, as consequential computations occur without a traceable output.

papers.title: Frustratingly Simple Black-Box Adaptation of Language Models via Logit Bias

summary.tldr: A black-box method learns a context-independent logit-bias vector for language model adaptation, improving performance on domain-specific tasks without fine-tuning or gradient access.
key_points: The method uses a single context-independent logit-bias vector, added at every decoding step, without modifying model weights or requiring gradients.
A KL-regularized reinforcement learning (RL) objective is used to characterize when a fixed logit-bias vector approximates optimal prefix-dependent correction.
A closed-form inverse-propensity estimator is derived from rollouts, rewards, and token probabilities for learning the logit bias.
Empirical results show improved performance on mathematical and reasoning benchmarks compared to base models, using fewer trainable parameters than fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: This lightweight logit-bias mechanism offers a simple, API-level control for adapting language models with minimal access requirements, addressing performance and privacy concerns.

papers.title: \k{appa}-LoRA: Condition Numbers Reveal Which LoRA Matrices Worth Updating

summary.tldr: K-LoRA optimizes LoRA fine-tuning by updating only matrices with the largest condition numbers, which are shown to contribute most to adaptation, reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.
key_points: Matrices with larger condition numbers contain underdeveloped directions that span richer subspaces and drive most performance gains in LoRA adaptation.
K-LoRA focuses LoRA updates on the top 50% of weight matrices ranked by condition number.
K-LoRA reduces trainable parameter count by 50%, fine-tuning time by 16.2% on average, and memory cost by 4.5% compared to standard LoRA.
The condition numbers of selected matrices consistently decrease over training, indicating targeted spectral rebalancing.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly reduces the computational and memory costs of LoRA fine-tuning, making it more practical for large models and resource-constrained environments.

papers.title: HiKV: Hierarchical Importance-Aware KV Cache with Hardware Acceleration for LLM Decoding

summary.tldr: HiKV is an algorithm-hardware co-design that addresses the LLM KV cache memory bottleneck by hierarchically compressing the KV cache and accelerating it with a reconfigurable importance sorter.
key_points: HiKV employs a two-stage algorithmic compression: Stage I evicts unimportant tokens within a fixed budget, and Stage II loads only significant elements of retained tokens.
The architectural component is a dedicated accelerator featuring a reconfigurable importance sorter that switches datapaths for the two compression stages.
HiKV achieves up to 7.95x speedup and 90% energy reduction in attention computation with a 1% accuracy loss.
Under iso-accuracy, HiKV reduces external memory accesses by 1.82-4.87x compared to other importance-based methods.
The specialized hardware components add 8% to the system area.
summary.why_it_matters: This method significantly improves LLM decoding efficiency by reducing memory and energy consumption while maintaining accuracy.

papers.title: Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation via Byte-Prefix Marginalization

summary.tldr: Byte-Prefix Marginalization (BPM) is introduced for cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation, re-expressing teacher next-token distributions in a shared byte space to preserve probability mass and align vocabularies.
key_points: BPM assigns teacher token probability to the longest student token whose byte representation is a prefix of the teacher token's bytes.
Unmatched probability mass is placed in an explicit residual category, ensuring mass preservation.
BPM exactly recovers the teacher-induced byte-prefix marginal when the prefix does not span multiple teacher tokens (over 99% of training positions).
It uses a mass-preserving, chain-factorized lower bound when prefixes span multiple teacher tokens.
BPM improved six-benchmark avg@8 by 3.7-6.6 points over strongest baselines using Qwen3-32B, GLM-Z1-9B-0414, and MiniMax-M2.7 as teachers.
summary.why_it_matters: This method enables effective consolidation of diverse open-weight language models into compact students, improving performance on mathematics and programming benchmarks.

papers.title: Scaling Native Multimodal Pre-Training From Scratch

summary.tldr: This research systematically characterizes scaling properties of native multimodal pre-training, demonstrating distinct compute laws for language and multimodal objectives and deriving an efficiency frontier for model configuration.
key_points: Minimal objective loss in native multimodal pre-training adheres to a predictable compute law, while compute-optimal model sizes and token counts scale as power laws.
Language and multimodal objectives exhibit distinct scaling behaviors; language allocation is invariant to data composition, but multimodal allocation is highly sensitive.
Text-heavy data mixtures become compute-efficient for multimodal objectives only at larger model scales, shifting optimal resource allocation towards greater model capacity.
An efficiency frontier is derived, specifying precise configurations of model size, token count, and data mixture based on data composition's influence on compute laws and allocation exponents.
Native multimodal pre-training induces positive cross-modal transfer, improving pure-text spatial reasoning and enabling robust multimodal in-context learning.
summary.why_it_matters: This empirical research provides essential groundwork for predictably scaling multimodal foundation models, enabling more efficient development and deployment.

papers.title: J-CoT: Chain-of-Thought in J-Space

summary.tldr: J-CoT introduces J-space, a vocabulary-indexed coordinate system, to represent intermediate reasoning states as J-thoughts, enabling recurrent computation without full verbalization or dense hidden state recurrence, outperforming existing latent-reasoning methods.
key_points: J-CoT uses J-space, a vocabulary-indexed coordinate system within hidden representations, for intermediate states.
Intermediate states are expressed as vocabulary-indexed coefficients (J-thoughts) at cycle boundaries.
J-thoughts are mapped back into the model's hidden representation for the next computational cycle.
J-CoT-Zero matches or exceeds the strongest latent-reasoning baseline on all evaluated benchmarks.
J-CoT-Train achieves the highest scores across mathematical, scientific, coding, and structured path-reasoning tasks.
summary.why_it_matters: This method improves language model reasoning by providing a more efficient and effective way to manage intermediate computational states compared to natural language or dense hidden vector propagation.

papers.title: MoE$^2$-LoRA: When MoE Models Meet MoE-style Low-Rank Adaptation

summary.tldr: MoE$^2$-LoRA introduces MoE-style low-rank adaptation for fine-tuning Mixture-of-Experts models, using a Routing-Conditioned Projection module and a global LoRA expert pool for improved efficiency and accuracy.
key_points: MoE$^2$-LoRA couples pretrained expert specialization with task-specific adaptivity via a dual-channel Routing-Conditioned Projection (RCP) module.
The RCP module reuses base router activations to inform LoRA routing.
A single global LoRA expert pool is shared across all layers, enabling model-wide adaptation.
The method aims to achieve prior reuse, dynamic adapter routing, and model-wide knowledge sharing.
MoE$^2$-LoRA achieves state-of-the-art downstream accuracy and stronger general capabilities on various MoE backbones.
summary.why_it_matters: This method provides a more efficient and effective parameter-efficient fine-tuning approach for Mixture-of-Experts models, improving their adaptability and performance on downstream tasks.

papers.title: SIREN (Luring LLMs onto the Rocks): PAIR-Driven Preference Manipulation in Web-RAG Recommenders

summary.tldr: SIREN is an automated attacker-judge method adapting the PAIR jailbreaking loop to manipulate LLM-generated recommendations by iteratively editing retrieved web pages to promote a chosen entity to rank 1.
key_points: SIREN uses an interpretable taxonomy of 23 content-poisoning techniques to edit a retrieved source, keeping other sources and their order fixed.
The method achieved rank 1 in 62 of 124 technique trials across two production Claude models and eight query-model contexts.
Reproducibility testing of successful payloads in fresh sessions yielded a mean success rate of 0.805.
Declarative ranking claims and seeded lists were generally more effective than directive-form injections, with effectiveness varying by target model.
summary.why_it_matters: This study demonstrates a controlled method for competitive rank manipulation in production LLMs, highlighting vulnerabilities in web-RAG recommenders.

infra.title: ModelExpress: Distributing Model Artifacts at the Speed of Light

summary.tldr: ModelExpress addresses the challenge of distributing large model checkpoints, which can be hundreds of gigabytes or a terabyte, across clusters for various operations like cold starts, autoscaling, and rolling updates.
key_points: Model checkpoints are growing to hundreds of gigabytes or a terabyte, increasing data transfer costs.
Frequent movement of model weights occurs during cold starts, autoscaling, rolling updates, and RL post-training.
summary.why_it_matters: Efficient distribution of large model artifacts is critical for managing operational costs and performance in AI model deployment and training workflows.

infra.title: Get started with OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna on Amazon Bedrock

summary.tldr: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models are now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, offering capabilities for agentic coding, long-horizon reasoning, and high-volume inference with AWS security and cost controls.
key_points: The GPT-5.6 family includes Sol (openai.gpt-5.6-sol) for autonomous coding and deep reasoning, Terra (openai.gpt-5.6-terra) for general-purpose production, and Luna (openai.gpt-5.6-luna) for high-volume, latency-sensitive workloads.

All three models support text and image input, text output, a 272K-token context window, and the OpenAI Responses API, accessible via the bedrock-mantle endpoint (https://bedrock-mantle.{region}.api.aws/openai/v1/responses).
Models support `none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, and `max` reasoning effort, allowing API integration consistency across models.
Inference runs within AWS IAM policies, VPCs, and CloudTrail logging, with in-Region processing for data residency; prompts and completions are not used for model training.
summary.why_it_matters: Developers can now access OpenAI's frontier models through a familiar API on Amazon Bedrock, integrating advanced AI capabilities with existing AWS infrastructure and security protocols.

vendors.title: Supporting ambitious external research through the Anthropic Economic Futures Research Fund

summary.tldr: Anthropic has committed $200 million to the Economic Futures Research Fund to support external research on interventions preparing society for AI's economic impacts, prioritizing large-scale projects and pilots.
key_points: Anthropic is committing $200 million to the Economic Futures Research Fund to support external research.
The fund will prioritize five research areas focused on interventions to make economies flexible and resilient, ensure shared AI benefits, and minimize disruption.
Projects will primarily be funded in the $5-30 million range, with a minimum of $1 million, and may exceed $30 million for high-potential-impact projects.
The fund seeks ambitious proposals, including large-scale Randomized Controlled Trials (RCTs), creative pilots, and program evaluations, with a global scope.
Research organizations are expected to share learnings publicly at key milestones to enable timely action.
summary.why_it_matters: This initiative aims to build an evidence base for effective interventions in an AI-transformed economy, guiding workers, firms, and governments in adaptation.
